newsitem.title: USA: Evidence Huang leaked classified info - report.
newsitem.headline: Evidence Huang leaked classified info - report.

text.p: Former key Democratic Party fund-raiser and Commerce Department official John Huang may have leaked classified economic information to an Asian corporate connection, a television network reported on Wednesday.

CBS News, citing sources, said the government had collected information by electronic eavesdropping devices suggesting that while Huang worked at the Commerce Department he passed classified trade secrets and other information to his former employer, Indonesia-based Lippo Group, an international company with ties to China.
House Rules Committee Chairman Gerald Solomon, interviewed on CBS, said he believed the information was the fuel needed to provoke a full investigation.

Attorney General Reno and FBI Director Louis Freeh gave senators an early read on this during an April visit to the Capitol, CBS said, but Solomon said he had since learned that Huang's access to classified information went deeper.
In a letter to Freeh, Solomon said Huang had access not only to Commerce Department information, but also sensitive State Department message traffic through a Commerce Department computer network.
The Senate committee investigating campaign fund-raising scandals will vote Thursday on a Republican proposal to offer a dozen witnesses immunity from prosecution in exchange for their testimony.

Sources close to the Senate governmental affairs committee said the witnesses were "lower level players who said they would not testify unless they received immunity and who could supply valuable information to the investigation."

The committee was investigating whether China and other foreign interests sought to influence U.S. foreign policy by helping President Bill Clinton and the Democratic Party with illegal political contributions in the 1996 election.
The Democratic Party promised to return some $3 million which were apparently illegally raised from foreign interests, mainly Asian corporations and businessmen.
